title: The optimisation that was not needed: measuring the gain afterwards

videos.script: You spent a day on an index, and the query got faster. Was it worth it? {{question}} Most optimisations are never asked that question. The change goes in, somebody says it feels quicker, and everyone moves on. {{feels}} But a database pays for every change it carries. An index is written on every insert. A cache must be kept honest. A clever query must be understood by the next person. {{cost}} This lesson takes one change that looks sensible, and measures it properly. Before and after, three runs each, the same workload. {{measure}} Then it asks whether the difference is bigger than the noise between runs. Often it is not. {{noise}} And then the arithmetic. How many times a day does this query run? How much time does each run save? Against what did we pay? {{sum}} The answer is allowed to be no. Removing a change that did not earn its place is as much a part of this job as adding one. {{no}}
